title: Congressman-Elect Amish Shah Puts Tariffs and Anti-Indian Hate at Top of His Agenda
excerpt: The Arizona Democrat, the first South Asian American elected to Congress from the state, says Indian-American entrepreneurs are being hurt by tariffs and that reclaiming Congress's tariff authority from the White House will be a top priority from January 3.
body:
• Dr Amish Shah, a Democrat, won Arizona's 1st Congressional District with 52.4% of the vote to Republican Jay Feely's 45.4%, becoming the first South Asian American to represent Arizona in the US Congress.
  • Shah, who takes office on January 3, said rolling back tariffs and restoring Congress's authority over them — taking it away from the White House — will be a top priority, saying the duties are hurting Indian entrepreneurs and raising prices for American households.
  • He pledged to confront rising anti-Indian hate, which he said has increased over the past six months to a year to a level he has never seen in his lifetime, and to join the India Caucus, which will have six members when the new Congress sits.
  • For Indian-American families and businesses: Shah's stated agenda pairs district issues — cost of living, healthcare affordability, and Arizona's water supply — with tariff relief and a public stand against hate directed at the community.

Indian-American Congressman-elect Dr Amish Shah has set out the agenda he will carry into the US House of Representatives: roll back tariffs, take tariff-setting authority away from the White House, and confront a rise in anti-Indian hate that he says the community itself has put at the top of its list. Shah spoke on Wednesday on the sidelines of a press conference organised by the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC) and to a group of Indian reporters, according to ANI.

A First for Arizona

Shah, a Democrat, defeated Republican Jay Feely to win Arizona's 1st Congressional District in the 2026 midterm elections, becoming the first South Asian American to represent Arizona in the US Congress. According to CNN's election results updated on November 10, with an estimated 99% of votes counted, Shah secured 52.4% of the vote to Feely's 45.4%. He assumes office on January 3.

Tariffs: "Take It Away From the White House"

Shah said members of the Indian-American community had raised two concerns above others: anti-India hate, and the impact of tariffs on Indian entrepreneurs and businesses. Tariffs that were repeatedly imposed and changed had hurt business owners, he said, and the duties were raising the cost of basic goods for American consumers.

"Rolling back those tariffs, reasserting Congress's authority over tariffs, and taking it away from the White House will be a top priority as well. We want to help all the small businesses, including all the ones in my district."

— Congressman-elect Amish Shah

He illustrated the point with a conversation with the owner of Pizza Heaven, a restaurant he frequents, who told him rising tomato prices driven by tariffs had forced her to raise pizza prices. Addressing the tariff dispute, he argued, could also help repair relations between Washington and New Delhi, which he described as strategic and economic partners. Shah said he plans to join the India Caucus, noting there will be six Indian-American members in the House from January 3, including Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi.

"Never Seen Anything Like It"

On anti-Indian hostility, Shah said he had seen an increase over the past six months to a year unlike anything he could recall in his lifetime, IANS reported. He described the comments as hurtful for a community whose members had created jobs, served in medicine, and contributed across the economy, and noted that some of the hostility had come from candidates for public office. He recalled comments directed at students cheering for their football team, saying he could imagine himself in their place during his years at Northwestern University. Elected officials, he said, should condemn such hostility, stand with affected communities, and examine legislative opportunities to improve security, including safety at religious sites.

The District Agenda

Alongside the community issues, Shah listed the priorities of his incoming term as the rising cost of living, the economy, healthcare affordability and access to coverage, water supply in his district, and tackling the corruption he said has caused economic hardship. His first test comes quickly: the new Congress convenes on January 3, and any move to reclaim tariff authority from the White House would require legislation through a chamber where his party's strength is still being counted.
